title: dual-autoscale-fallback-and-driver-health-module-for-gpu-node-pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Private (VPC) customers running large models require predictable capacity and graceful fallbacks when preferred autoscaling (Karpenter) is temporarily unavailable. Current terraform modules cover basic GPU nodepool provisioning and autoscaler wiring, but we need a composable module that: 1) wires an ASG fallback for nodegroups managed by Karpenter (dual-mode fallback), 2) runs driver-level preflight and continuous health checks (NVIDIA driver, CUDA, NVSM), 3) supports controlled upgrades (canary pool, blue-green + cordon/drain policy) and 4) exposes observability hooks for Console (per-node metrics, per-pool cost breakdowns, upgrade traces).

Scope: Implement a Terraform module for Redwood Private that provisions a GPU node pool abstraction supporting two lifecycle modes: "preferred" Karpenter-managed ephemeral scaling, and an ASG-backed fallback pool that is auto-qualified and can be used when Karpenter capacity is constrained or when maintenance/upgrade windows require stable instances. The module will include user-configurable upgrade strategy (canary, rolling, blue-green), automated NVidia driver preflight scripts, healthcheck binaries invoked by cloud-init and a systemd probe, and Terraform outputs/labels for Redwood Console integration.

Design highlights:
- Module inputs: node_role_arn, subnet_ids, instance_types_preferred (for karpenter), instance_type_asg_fallback, gpu_profile (vram/cuda), max_price_strategy (spot|on_demand|fallback), taints_for_workloads, node_labels (map as JSON string), upgrade_strategy (canary|rolling|blue-green), canary_fraction (percent), min_ready_seconds.
- Dual autoscale behavior: create an ASG (with launch template) sized to minimum stable capacity and marked as fallback via tags; wire an optional lifecycle hook that cordons Karpenter scheduling to prefer karpenter-created nodes; provide an operator flag to flip traffic to ASG pool.
- Driver preflight & healthchecks: cloud-init installs driver + nvmlprobe; systemd unit nv-driver-health.service runs start-time preflight, then registers with instance metadata (custom tag) and exposes a /healthz endpoint on localhost via socat for agent scraping; failure policy supports node cordon + restart-driver + if unrecoverable, mark node for replacement by ASG.
- Upgrade strategy: canary pool created by setting a small canary ASG or using node selectors to target canary taint; run sample inference smoke tests (python script using perf harness) against canary nodes; on success, proceed to rolling or blue-green depending on upgrade_strategy input. Provide explicit terraform plan steps to avoid accidental simultaneous drain of all GPU capacity.
- Observability & alerts: emit Prometheus metrics (nv_driver_ok, driver_restart_count, cuda_compat_ok), log to CloudWatch/Elasticsearch for Private control plane ingestion, and add Console-friendly outputs (prometheus_label, nodepool_id) for per-route dashboards. Alert playbooks for: driver regressions, high restart-rate, karpenter eviction surge, ASG failover activation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module can create a Karpenter-preferred pool plus ASG fallback in a customer VPC with sample HCL below.
- Driver preflight runs as part of instance boot and marks instance healthy before node joins cluster.
- Canary upgrade path executes smoke tests automatically and aborts on failures with clear logs.
- Failover test: simulated Karpenter control-plane outage causes ASG fallback to take traffic within documented SLO (under 60s for new capacity allocation + 90s for node readiness).
- Terraform module documented with variables, outputs, example usage, and a migration guide from the legacy gpu-nodepool module.

Out-of-scope: full KMS/HSM integration (we provide hooks and documented variables but not an internal KMS implementation), detailed per-application eviction policies (left to workload teams).
acceptance_criteria: Module provisions Karpenter-preferred nodes + ASG fallback in a sample VPC using provided example HCL
Boot-time driver preflight must pass before node registers; failing nodes are cordoned and replaced
Canary upgrade sequence runs smoke tests and prevents rollout on regression
ASG fallback activation tested by simulating Karpenter outage; documented failover timing within SLO
Module outputs include labels/ids for Console integration and Prometheus metric labels
example_usage_hcl:
module "gpu_dual_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//gpu_dual_pool?ref=private-2026"
  node_role_arn = var.node_role_arn
  subnet_ids = var.private_subnets
  instance_types_preferred = ["p4d.24xlarge", "g5.12xlarge"]
  instance_type_asg_fallback = "g5.4xlarge"
  gpu_profile = "v100-32gb"
  upgrade_strategy = "canary"
  canary_fraction = 10
  max_price_strategy = "on_demand_fallback"
}
test_plan: terratest suite (go) validates module against a small staging VPC: create/destroy and drift detection
driver-functional tests: run sample model inference on booted nodes using perf harness
failure-injection: stop karpenter-controller to validate ASG fallback activation and timing
upgrade-simulation: deploy canary image with intentional driver regression to validate abort path
comments: 2025-11-15 - Aisha Patel: Initial discovery notes posted and design skeleton created. Confirmed kernel/driver compatibility matrix required for canary decisions.
2025-12-02 - Marco Ruiz: POC cloud-init script uploaded to the design doc. Early smoke tests show NVML access works after deferred module load (systemd drop-in).

2026-01-20 - Emily Wong (SRE): Reviewed healthcheck approach; suggested adding a short-lived local TCP probe to satisfy Console liveness scraping and to reduce false positives from transient modprobe failures.

2026-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented ASG lifecycle hook to tag ephemeral instances and added terraform output 'fallback_active' boolean. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/442
2026-03-03 - Security review (preliminary): Request to document KMS key usage and to add least-privilege IAM policy for driver installation. Filed follow-up ENG-204901 for IAM refinement.

2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Ran staged failover test; observed ASG scale up within 48s but full CUDA readiness took 77s on p4d. Notes added to Confluence and canary_fraction recommendation adjusted to 15% for p4d families.
next_steps: Complete terratest harness and CI job (expected 2 sprints)
Iterate on cloud-init idempotency for mixed instance types (edge-case seen on older AMIs)
Add Console dashboard prototype and per-node metrics ingestion route
